verdict.headline: Yes — Vietnamese passport holders need a visa.
verdict.sub: Apply according to your registered residence: KVAC Hanoi, KVAC Ho Chi Minh City, or the Korean Consulate General in Da Nang. Check the current jurisdiction and appointment instructions before visiting.

highlights.title: Allow time for visa assessment
highlights.body: Published individual tourist processing times are 16 working days in Hanoi and 18 working days in Ho Chi Minh City. Weekends and holidays are excluded; additional checks can take longer. These are published estimates, not guaranteed deadlines. Da Nang applicants should confirm separately.

highlights.title: Financial evidence — follow your office's checklist
highlights.body: Use the checklist for your office and application category. Hanoi's current individual C-3-9 checklist requests bank statements for the latest 3 months, plus salary records for employees. Include residence and family documents when applicable; translation and certification requirements vary.

tldr: Ordinary Vietnamese passports are not eligible for K-ETA. For a normal mainland tourist trip, obtain a visa; K-ETA cannot replace it and is not an extra application after receiving your visa.

items.q: Do Vietnamese citizens need a visa for Korea?
items.a: Ordinary Vietnamese passports are not eligible for K-ETA. For a normal mainland tourist trip, obtain a visa; K-ETA cannot replace it and is not an extra application after receiving your visa.

items.q: How much money do I need to prove?
items.a: Use the checklist for your office and application category. Hanoi's current individual C-3-9 checklist requests bank statements for the latest 3 months, plus salary records for employees. Include residence and family documents when applicable; translation and certification requirements vary.

Short-stay single-entry visa: USD 20; multiple-entry: USD 80. KVAC Hanoi and HCMC add VND 390,000 per application, excluding optional services. Confirm the payable currency and current total at your office; the KVAC service charge is not a Da Nang consular charge.

items.q: I'm going on a company incentive trip — simpler?
items.a: Group travel and multiple-entry visas have their own checklists and eligibility. Do not assume a company's guarantee automatically removes your financial-document requirement.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
items.a: A short-term tourist entering with a visa must submit the e-Arrival Card unless a separate exemption applies, such as holding a valid Korean residence card. Check the official navigator for your documents.

items.q: Can Vietnamese travelers visit Jeju without a visa?
items.a: Vietnamese ordinary-passport tourists can use the separate Jeju visa-free program for up to 30 days, subject to entry assessment. Arrive directly at Jeju from overseas by air or sea and stay on Jeju. An itinerary entering Korea through Seoul or Busan is not covered. Going to the mainland requires the appropriate visa or prior immigration permission; admission is not guaranteed.

items.q: How long does a Korea visa take to process?
items.a: Published individual tourist processing times are 16 working days in Hanoi and 18 working days in Ho Chi Minh City. Weekends and holidays are excluded; additional checks can take longer. These are published estimates, not guaranteed deadlines. Da Nang applicants should confirm separately.

items.q: Do children need their own Korea visa?
items.a: Yes — every traveler, including children, needs their own visa. A minor's application is submitted with a parent's supporting documents and proof of the family relationship.

items.q: Do Vietnamese travelers need K-ETA as well as a visa?
items.a: Ordinary Vietnamese passports are not eligible for K-ETA. For a normal mainland tourist trip, obtain a visa; K-ETA cannot replace it and is not an extra application after receiving your visa.

items.q: Does a US or Japanese visa allow visa-free transit in Korea?
items.a: A qualifying visa or residence permit for the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand or a listed European country may allow B-2 transit for up to 30 days on an eligible onward/return route. A Japanese visa alone is not in the current third-country transit list. You need a confirmed departure within 30 days and must meet immigration-history, routing and visa-document conditions; merely owning a visa or taking a Vietnam–Korea round trip is insufficient. Verify your complete itinerary with immigration and the airline.
